subject: Runbook & measurement protocol — Strata analytics SLO qualification
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Fiona Grant <fiona.grant@strata-analytics.com>, Paul Jackson <paul.jackson@strata-analytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Runbook & measurement protocol — Strata analytics SLO qualification

Hi Fiona / Paul,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good alignment on goals. Short recap + proposed next steps so we can get the qualification run scheduled: 

1) Target SLOs (please confirm):
   - Latency: p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 150ms, p99 <= 350ms (end-to-end token generation for 512-token responses)
   - Throughput: steady-state 800 req/s (aggregate), burst to 2k req/s for up to 30s
   - Concurrency: support 24 concurrent streams per shard with live KV cache
   - Streaming: yes — partial token flushing required (we'll validate inter-token latency and chunk sizes)

2) Measurement scope:
   - Warm vs cold: primary acceptance is warm-start (with KV cache warm). We will also run a 30-minute cold-start window to surface steady-state ramp behaviors.
   - Payload mix: please share representative prompt length distribution and ratio of 'short' (<=128 tokens) vs 'long' (>128 tokens) calls.

3) Deliverables we need from your side:
   - Prompt bundle (sample prompts & expected scoring heuristics)
   - Any pairing rules for tool-calls / function-calls that affect tokenization
   - Target test window and preferred windows for noisy production traffic (if you want isolated runs)

4) Redwood will provide:
   - Draft measurement spec (attached: redwood_measurement_spec_v0.3.md)
   - A small reproducibility harness + instructions (attached: redwood_harness_quickstart.pdf) we can run in your environment or run from our Dedicated pool, whichever you prefer.
   - Repro steps to validate p50/p95/p99 and per-token streaming latencies.

Can you confirm the SLO numbers (or give your target bands), and upload the prompt bundle and any sample payload stats to the Drive link below? Once we have the prompt bundle we can propose a 3x2-hour window for qualification runs.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d-strata-harness

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Lead Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Fiona Grant <fiona.grant@strata-analytics.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Paul Jackson <paul.jackson@strata-analytics.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Runbook & measurement protocol — Strata analytics SLO qualification

Sofia — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items and attaching our prompt set.

- SLO band: we'll aim for p50 <= 50ms, p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 400ms (we're willing to tighten if the measurement shows headroom).
- Throughput: target steady 500 req/s (initial), with a 1k req/s burst profile. We want to validate up to 1.5k to understand risks.
- Concurrency: our traffic usually hits 18 concurrent long-lived streams for chat sessions; short requests spike concurrency higher.
- Streaming: yes. We require partial responses to be flushed no more than 60ms between non-empty chunks for interactive sessions.

Attached: strata_prompt_bundle_v1.jsonl (4k prompts across 6 categories), and a spreadsheet with token-length distribution. We put a short notes column describing expected acceptability heuristics we use.

We'll confirm preferred test windows by EOD Monday. For security, can you confirm whether the harness run requires IP allowlisting or a temp key?

Thanks,
Fiona
Fiona Grant
Head of Platform Integrations | Strata Analytics
[attachment: strata_prompt_bundle_v1.jsonl]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Fiona Grant <fiona.grant@strata-analytics.com>, Paul Jackson <paul.jackson@strata-analytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-19T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Runbook & measurement protocol — Strata analytics SLO qualification

Fiona — perfect, thanks for the bundle and distribution. Quick answers: 

- Harness access: we support both modes. Option A: we run from our Dedicated pool and publish signed measurement artifacts (no IP allowlist needed; you'll get artifacts and logs). Option B: we provide a short-lived token + a small Docker harness you can run inside your network (this will require IP allowlist for the callback endpoints if you select streaming validation).

- IP allowlist details and a minimal ACL manifest are in the quickstart PDF. For Option B we will need a CIDR range (we can provide suggested ranges).

Proposed measurement protocol (high level):
  * Phase 1 (sanity): 30m low qps smoke run — confirm end-to-end correctness and basic latencies.
  * Phase 2 (warm steady-state): 2 x 1-hour steady-state runs at target throughput (we'll do one at 500 qps and one at your target 800 qps if you want to test both). Metrics: p50/p95/p99, token-level inter-chunk latency, 99.9th percentile connection drops.
  * Phase 3 (stress): 3 x 10-minute bursts up to 1.5k qps to validate graceful degradation and routing fallbacks.

A couple of measurement details Marcus/Neha and I discussed internally:
- We'll measure token-latency for streaming as the time between first-byte of chunk N and first-byte of chunk N+1, and report chunk sizes (bytes/tokens).
- For concurrency we will measure active KV sessions and the per-shard queue length to understand headroom.

Next step: can you confirm which of the two harness modes you prefer and share a 48-hour window (range) so Marcus can schedule the Dedicated pool/pre-warm shards?

Sofia

Subject: Re: Runbook & measurement protocol — Strata analytics SLO qualification

Fiona / team — a couple of internal technical notes to make the measurement reproducible and helpful for ops handoff: 

- Warm versus cold: please note that 'warm' in our runtime means the KV cache has been populated with typical context keys for at least 10 minutes of representative traffic. We'll provide a pre-warm script that replays ~5-10k representative prompts at low qps prior to the steady-state window.
- Traffic generator: we recommend using our generator (included in the quickstart) to preserve realistic inter-arrival times and payload tokenization; synthetic flat qps floods give different amplification behavior.
- Measurement anchors: label each run with run_id and seed (we'll embed in responses) so we can cross-check traces and logs for exact reproducibility.
- Network jitter: we will capture client-side and edge-side timestamps to isolate network vs inference latency; please allow UDP ping traces during runs if possible.

If you choose Option A (Redwood-run), we will: allocate dedicated shards, pre-warm KV caches, and deliver a full artifact bundle (csv/time-series + per-request traces + raw token timings). If Option B, we will validate the harness output together in a short post-run call.

Will start reserving time on Wed/Thu unless you ask otherwise.

Marcus
Principal SRE — Redwood Inference

[internal note: include pre-warm script + run_id convention in the run artifacts]

Thanks all — we reviewed internally and are comfortable with Option A (Redwood-run) for the initial qualification. A few asks before you reserve: 

- Please provide a one-page summary of data handling during the run (retention, logs, any PII handling) and your SOC2/Security contact so our security team can triage.
- We'll need the pre-warm script and run_id format at least 24 hours before the run window.
- Attached is our audit questionnaire (strata_audit_questions_2027.xlsx) — we've flagged the security fields we expect answers to pre-run.

Once we have the one-pager and pre-warm script we'll confirm the Wed/Thu window.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Paul
VP Product — Strata Analytics
